question: Dandruff flakes and head-louse nits both slide easily off the hair shaft when pulled, making them difficult to distinguish on examination.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. Nits are firmly cemented to the hair shaft with chitinous glue and cannot be simply brushed or pulled off, whereas dandruff flakes slide off freely. This is the single most useful bedside test to distinguish the two — if it slides off easily, it is not a nit.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. Dandruff scales and hair casts slide freely off the shaft, whereas nits are cemented by a sleeve of chitinous glue and resist removal. This simple bedside test — does it slide off? — is the most reliable way to tell nits from dandruff and avoids unnecessary pediculicide treatment.
